title: Pentagon UAP files part 8: Radar track analysis and more
site_name: EarthSky | Updates on your cosmos and world
excerpt: The U.S. government released the 8th batch of Pentagon UAP files on November 20, 2026. They include 3 videos from the Middle East and numerous documents.
content:
• The U.S. Pentagon released the 8th batch of its UAP files on November 20, 2026.
  • This Pentagon UAP files release contains 43 new files altogether. Among these, 40 are documents and three are videos.
  • The release is part of a continuing rollout of formerly classified files, every few weeks. So far, there’s still been no “smoking gun” to show that alien craft are visiting Earth. But the files are interesting!

8th batch of Pentagon UAP files

The U.S. Pentagon released its 1st batch of declassified UAP/UFO materials on May 8, 2026. On Friday, November 20, it released batch 8. There are 43 new files in batch 8, 40 PDF documents (some with images) and three videos. There are no audio or separate image files this time around, however.

Some of the documents are older again, but others are from this year.

And as has been the pattern for these releases, they are a mixed bag of old and previously known material and newer material. Do the releases prove aliens exist, or that alien craft are visiting Earth? No. Not so far, across any of the eight releases.

As usual, Sean Parnell, Assistant to the Secretary of Defense for Public Affairs and Chief Pentagon Spokesman, said in a statement:

Today, the Department of War is publishing the 8th release of declassified and historical Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) files as part of the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE). The collection continues to be housed on WAR.GOV/UFO, and the Department will release additional files on a rolling basis.

The Department of War and our agency partners are actively working on the next release of UAP files. The 8th release of UAP files is available now on WAR.GOV/UFO.

For context, the government released a 2nd batch on May 22, a 3rd batch on June 12, the 4th batch on July 10, the 5th batch on August 7, the 6th batch on September 18 and the 7th batch of the Pentagon UAP files on October 23, all in 2026. 

1st analysis of radar tracks

One of the more interesting cases in this batch is a series of unusual radar tracks in the western U.S. from 2023. A civil air-surveillance radar system recorded eight detections over 84 seconds at an estimated altitude of 55.000-70.000 feet (16,760-21,300 meter).

The distance between the tracks was 38.5 miles (62 km). The analysis suggested that if it was just one object causing the tracks, then it had a groundspeed of 1,650 mph (2,700 kph), or approximately Mach 2.5 at the reported altitude.

Additionally, there was also an apparent 39-degree counterclockwise change in bearing after approximately 48 seconds.

The 12-second radar sweep interval, however, is not sufficient to independently establish that all eight reported detections originated from the same object or represent a continuous track.

3 videos from the Middle East in Pentagon UAP files

There are only three videos in this release, all from the Middle East.

The 1st video is from the United States Central Command, which submitted a report of an unidentified anomalous phenomenon (UAP) to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO). The 20-second-long footage is from a U.S. military platform in 2020.

The object (or area of contrast as the DoD calls it), a tiny dot in the video, passes by a warship.

The 2nd video is also from the United States Central Command and submitted to AARO. It consists of 54 seconds of video footage from an electro-optical and infrared system aboard a U.S. military platform in 2026.

It shows multiple objects, dots again, moving over the ocean.

The 3rd video, again from the United States Central Command and submitted to AARO, is 13 seconds long. An electro-optical and infrared system aboard a U.S. Military platform obtained the footage in 2023.

It is similar to the 1st two videos, showing a small dot-like object. In this one, however, the object makes sudden, sharp changes in direction.

Assessment of national security issues relating to ‘Flying Saucers,’ 1952

This document from 1952 is interesting. It is a memorandum from S. Q. Reber, Assistant Director for Intelligence Coordination, to the Deputy Director (Intelligence). It provides an assessment of national security issues relating to “flying saucers.”

And there is an interesting reference to psychological warfare in the conclusion. It says:

It is far too early in view of the present state of our knowledge regarding Flying Saucers for psychological warfare planners to start planning how the United States might use U.S. Flying Saucers against the enemy.

Lockheed UAP report, 1953

There is also the full UAP report from leading Lockheed aerospace engineer Kelly Johnson (associated with the spy planes U-2 and SR-71) and Lockheed’s top test pilots/engineers. The incident occurred near Agoura and Point Mugu, California, on December 16, 1953. The report description states:

This report is significant, due to Johnson’s reputation as one of the foremost aerospace engineers in American history, and his virtually unmatched familiarity with high-performance aircraft.

Johnson reported observing a dark, elliptical object from his ranch west of Agoura at approximately 5 p.m. He initially considered whether it might be a cloud or smoke trail; he reported that it appeared stationary for several minutes before moving westward and disappearing.

At about the same time, personnel aboard a Lockheed test flight reported seeing an object in the vicinity of Point Mugu while flying off the southern California coast. Their accounts described a similar stationary, dark, wing-like or elongated object that also moved westward and disappeared from view.

Johnson himself said:

I should state that for at least five years I have definitely believed in the possibility that flying saucers exist; this in spite of a good deal of kidding from my technical associates. Having seen this particular object on December 16th, I am now more firmly convinced than ever that such devices exist, and I have some highly technical converts in this belief as of that date.

BAASS 10-month report

The July 2009 10-month report from BAASS (Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Studies) is also included in this batch. It’s long, at 538 pages. The report was part of a Defense Intelligence Agency program, AAWSAP (Advanced Aerospace Weapon Systems Applications Program), funded by Congress. Senator Harry Reid pushed for the program, to study potential future aerospace threats and UAP.

The report highlighted the need for:

… a highly secure underground vault to store hardware and biological samples from the corporate world and/or from private individuals and groups located elsewhere, including Brazil.

The report added:

It was recognized by the BAASS administrator that there was no highly secure facility at BAASS to store exotic material or tissue that the organization could obtain. Accordingly, the BAASS administrator designed an underground facility to be located in North Las Vegas at the Bigelow Aerospace facility.

It would be buried under 15 to 20 feet of dirt and feature a 5,000-square-foot (465-square-meter) vault with 3-foot-thick (1-meter-thick) walls and a thick steel door. It would be camouflaged on the ground. The facility was reportedly never built, however.

Bottom line: The U.S. government released the 8th batch of Pentagon UAP files on November 20, 2026. They include three videos from the Middle East and numerous documents.
